title: Animal Tissue Master Practice Exam (50 Questions - Mixed MCQs & MSQs)

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC1] In Practice Exam (Topic 1), identify the French anatomist who defined 21 primary tissue types without microscopic aid:
questions.explanation: Xavier Bichat coined the term tissue and defined 21 primary tissue classes.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC1] In Practice Exam (Topic 1), microscopic investigation of animal tissues was systematically pioneered by which biologist?
questions.explanation: Marcello Malpighi pioneered microscopic histology.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC1] In Practice Exam (Topic 1), true tissue level of organization first evolved in which invertebrate phylum?
questions.explanation: Tissue grade organization originated in Coelenterates (Hydra).

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC1] In Practice Exam (Topic 1), embryonic mesoderm gives origin to which pair of primary tissues?
questions.explanation: Connective tissue and muscle arise from embryonic mesoderm.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC1] In Practice Exam (Topic 1), which primary tissue type originates from all three germ layers (Ectoderm, Mesoderm, Endoderm)?
questions.explanation: Epithelia derive from ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC1] In Practice Exam (Topic 1), the non-cellular basement membrane underlying epithelial sheets contains basal lamina and:
questions.explanation: Basement membrane = Basal lamina + Reticular lamina.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC1] In Practice Exam (Topic 1), avascular epithelial sheets obtain metabolic nutrients primarily via:
options: A) Direct intra-epithelial capillary blood flow
B) Simple diffusion from underlying connective tissue blood vessels
C) Active transport from lumen air space
questions.answer: B) Simple diffusion from underlying connective tissue blood vessels
questions.explanation: Epithelial cells depend on nutrient diffusion across the basement membrane.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC1] In Practice Exam (Topic 1 - MSQ), select all historical milestones established in animal histology: (Select all that apply)
options: A) Xavier Bichat defined 21 primary tissue types without microscope
B) Marcello Malpighi pioneered microscopic tissue investigation
C) Mayer coined the term 'Histology' in 1819
D) True tissue level first evolved in Phylum Coelenterata
answers: A) Xavier Bichat defined 21 primary tissue types without microscope
B) Marcello Malpighi pioneered microscopic tissue investigation
C) Mayer coined the term 'Histology' in 1819
D) True tissue level first evolved in Phylum Coelenterata
questions.explanation: Bichat, Malpighi, Mayer, and Coelenterate evolution represent foundational histology milestones.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC1] In Practice Exam (Topic 1 - MSQ), select all primary tissue classes in complex animals: (Select all that apply)
options: E) Vascular Tissue as fifth primary class
questions.explanation: 4 primary tissues: Epithelial, Connective, Muscular, Nervous.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC1] In Practice Exam (Topic 1 - MSQ), select all embryonic germ layers giving rise to Epithelial Tissues: (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Epithelium arises from Ectoderm, Mesoderm, and Endoderm.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC2] In Practice Exam (Topic 2), simple squamous epithelium lining blood vessels is called:
questions.explanation: Endothelium lines blood and lymph vessels.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC2] In Practice Exam (Topic 2), simple cuboidal epithelium with microvilli brush border occurs in:
options: B) Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT) of nephron
questions.answer: B) Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT) of nephron
questions.explanation: Renal PCT features simple cuboidal brush-bordered epithelium.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC2] In Practice Exam (Topic 2), mucus-secreting unicellular exocrine glands in stomach mucosa are called:
questions.explanation: Goblet cells are unicellular exocrine glands.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC2] In Practice Exam (Topic 2), pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium is characteristically found lining the:
questions.explanation: Trachea and bronchi are lined by pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC2] In Practice Exam (Topic 2), non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium lines which moist cavity?
questions.explanation: Non-keratinized stratified squamous lines moist internal cavities.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC2] In Practice Exam (Topic 2), distensible plastic urothelium featuring surface umbrella cells lines the:
questions.explanation: Transitional epithelium (urothelium) lines the urinary bladder.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC2] In Practice Exam (Topic 2), cell junctions that seal adjacent cell membranes preventing fluid leakage are:
questions.explanation: Tight junctions form occluding barriers preventing fluid leakage.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC2] In Practice Exam (Topic 2 - MSQ), select all anatomical locations lined by Simple Cuboidal Epithelium: (Select all that apply)
options: C) Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT) of nephron
answers: C) Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT) of nephron
questions.explanation: Simple cuboidal lines thyroid follicles, gland ducts, renal PCT, and ovary surface.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC2] In Practice Exam (Topic 2 - MSQ), select all cell junction types connecting adjacent epithelial cells: (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Epithelial junctions include Tight, Adherens, Desmosome, and Gap junctions.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC2] In Practice Exam (Topic 2 - MSQ), select all characteristics of Transitional Epithelium (Urothelium): (Select all that apply)
options: C) High stretch capability without cell separation
D) Lines urinary bladder, ureters, and renal pelvis
E) Keratinized dead cell stratum corneum
answers: C) High stretch capability without cell separation
D) Lines urinary bladder, ureters, and renal pelvis
questions.explanation: Urothelium is a distensible compound epithelium lining the urinary tract.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC3] In Practice Exam (Topic 3), matrix-producing connective tissue cells synthesizing collagen and elastin fibers are:
questions.explanation: Fibroblasts synthesize fibers and ground substance.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC3] In Practice Exam (Topic 3), histamine, heparin, and serotonin are released during inflammation by:
questions.explanation: Mast cells release histamine, heparin, and serotonin.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC3] In Practice Exam (Topic 3), tissue macrophages residing in loose connective tissue proper are:
questions.explanation: Histocytes are phagocytic macrophages in connective tissue proper.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC3] In Practice Exam (Topic 3), antibody-producing plasma cells differentiate from activated:
questions.explanation: Plasma cells derive from antigen-stimulated B-lymphocytes.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC3] In Practice Exam (Topic 3), tendons attaching skeletal muscle to bone consist of:
options: A) Dense Regular White Fibrous CT
questions.answer: A) Dense Regular White Fibrous CT
questions.explanation: Tendons are composed of dense regular white fibrous CT.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC3] In Practice Exam (Topic 3), tough shock-absorbing cartilage in intervertebral discs lacking perichondrium is:
questions.explanation: Fibrocartilage has thick collagen bundles and forms intervertebral discs.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC3] In Practice Exam (Topic 3), the structural unit of compact bone comprising Haversian canal and lamellae is:
questions.explanation: The osteon is the functional structural unit of compact bone.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC3] In Practice Exam (Topic 3 - MSQ), select all cell types residing in Loose Areolar Connective Tissue matrix: (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Areolar CT matrix contains fibroblasts, mast cells, histocytes, and plasma cells.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC3] In Practice Exam (Topic 3 - MSQ), select all Granulocytic Leucocytes in circulating blood: (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Granulocytes = Neutrophils, Eosinophils, Basophils.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC3] In Practice Exam (Topic 3 - MSQ), select all formed blood elements: (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Formed blood elements comprise RBCs, WBCs, and Platelets.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC4] In Practice Exam (Topic 4), skeletal muscle fibers are described histologically as:
options: A) Involuntary, unstriated, uninucleated fusiform cells
questions.explanation: Skeletal muscle is voluntary, striated, and syncytial.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC4] In Practice Exam (Topic 4), smooth muscle cells lining the gastrointestinal visceral wall are:
options: B) Involuntary, non-striated, fusiform spindle cells
questions.answer: B) Involuntary, non-striated, fusiform spindle cells
questions.explanation: Smooth muscle cells are spindle-shaped, uninucleated, involuntary, and unstriated.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC4] In Practice Exam (Topic 4), structural intercalated discs with gap junctions and desmosomes are unique to:
questions.explanation: Intercalated discs connect cardiac muscle cells into a functional syncytium.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC4] In Practice Exam (Topic 4), the functional contractile unit of a myofibril bounded by Z-lines is:
questions.explanation: The sarcomere is the contractile unit of myofibrils between Z-lines.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC4] In Practice Exam (Topic 4), during skeletal muscle contraction, which band length remains CONSTANT?
questions.explanation: A-band represents thick myosin length and remains constant during contraction.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC4] In Practice Exam (Topic 4), calcium ions released from sarcoplasmic reticulum bind directly to:
questions.explanation: Ca2+ binds Troponin C, triggering tropomyosin shift to unmask actin binding sites.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC4] In Practice Exam (Topic 4), red muscle fibers resist fatigue because they contain abundant:
questions.explanation: Red muscle has high myoglobin and mitochondria for slow-twitch aerobic respiration.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC4] In Practice Exam (Topic 4 - MSQ), select all characteristics belonging to Skeletal Muscle histology: (Select all that apply)
options: B) Multinucleated syncytium with peripheral nuclei
C) Cross-striated A and I bands
E) Intercalated discs with gap junctions
answers: B) Multinucleated syncytium with peripheral nuclei
C) Cross-striated A and I bands
questions.explanation: Skeletal muscle is voluntary, syncytial, striated, and fatigable.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC4] In Practice Exam (Topic 4 - MSQ), select all features distinguishing Cardiac Muscle from Skeletal Muscle: (Select all that apply)
options: B) Branched cardiocytes with central nuclei
C) Intercalated discs providing electrical coupling
answers: B) Branched cardiocytes with central nuclei
C) Intercalated discs providing electrical coupling
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle is involuntary, branched, fatigue-resistant, and connected by intercalated discs.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC4] In Practice Exam (Topic 4 - MSQ), select all connective tissue sheaths organizing skeletal muscle blocks: (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Muscle sheaths = Endomysium, Perimysium, Epimysium.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC5] In Practice Exam (Topic 5), the metabolic cell body of a neurone containing the nucleus is the:
questions.explanation: Cyton (Soma) is the main cell body of a neurone.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC5] In Practice Exam (Topic 5), Nissl's granules in cyton and dendrites consist of clumps of:
options: B) Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum and free Ribosomes
questions.answer: B) Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum and free Ribosomes
questions.explanation: Nissl's granules are RER and free ribosomes synthesizing protein.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC5] In Practice Exam (Topic 5), Nissl's granules are strictly ABSENT in:
questions.explanation: Nissl's granules are absent in axon hillock and axon.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC5] In Practice Exam (Topic 5), saltatory nerve impulse propagation leaps along myelinated axons at:
questions.explanation: Action potentials jump from Node of Ranvier to Node of Ranvier.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC5] In Practice Exam (Topic 5), which CNS neuroglia construct the Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB)?
questions.explanation: Astrocytes form perivascular end-feet creating the Blood-Brain Barrier.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC5] In Practice Exam (Topic 5), myelin sheath in the Central Nervous System (CNS) is synthesized by:
questions.explanation: Oligodendrocytes form CNS myelin; Schwann cells form PNS myelin.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC5] In Practice Exam (Topic 5), phagocytic macrophage defense neuroglia in the CNS are:
questions.explanation: Microglia act as tissue macrophages defending the CNS.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC5] In Practice Exam (Topic 5 - MSQ), select all neuroglial cells residing in the Central Nervous System (CNS): (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: CNS neuroglia: Astrocytes, Oligodendrocytes, Microglia, Ependymal. Schwann = PNS.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC5] In Practice Exam (Topic 5 - MSQ), select all neuroglial cells residing in the Peripheral Nervous System (PNS): (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: PNS neuroglia include Schwann cells and Satellite cells.

questions.stem: [Master Practice Exam - TOPIC5] In Practice Exam (Topic 5 - MSQ), select all anatomical locations containing Bipolar Neurones: (Select all that apply)
options: C) Inner ear vestibular and cochlear organs
answers: C) Inner ear vestibular and cochlear organs
questions.explanation: Bipolar neurones occur in retina, olfactory mucosa, and inner ear.
